I have farmed this small plot all my life, and my mother taught me how to care for these plants before me. This land is only 0.08 hectares, with my enset and the coffee bushes my husband planted long ago. I will not buy chemical fertilizer — one bag costs too much and is too big for this little plot, and I do not have that kind of money sitting in my house. Instead, I will carry manure from my cows and compost from my kitchen and spread it around the plants with my hands, the way my family always did. I do not need seed because these are old plants, not a new field, and if one dies I replace it with a sucker from my own garden. I do not use spray or medicine on them — if I see pests, I pick them off myself. The rain feeds them; I have no pump or pipe. My daughter comes to help me when her own work allows, so between us we will spend about 20 days on this plot weeding, mulching, and harvesting this season. I have no cash to pay outside workers.
